title: Enterprise onboarding, integration, escalation, and QBR playbook
author: Aisha Malik
body:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended process for enterprise onboarding, system integration, escalation handling, known issues and workarounds, and Quarterly Business Review (QBR) materials. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and account stakeholders. The goal is to ensure consistent, measurable, and auditable onboarding and post-sales operations for Dedicated and Private deployments as well as high-touch hosted customers.

Audience:
- Customer Success Managers
- Solutions Engineers
- Support Engineers (Tier 1–3)
- Professional Services and Implementation partners
- Account executive and sales engineering stakeholders

Prerequisites and gating:
- Signed contract or PO and onboarding acceptance (owner: Finance / Sales)
- Customer has completed the security questionnaire or executed a required NDA (owner: Security/Legal)
- For Private/Dedicated: network readiness checklist completed and verified (owner: SE)
- Assigned CSM, SE, and Technical Lead (owner: Customer Success)

High-level onboarding phases:
1) Kickoff (0–2 weeks):
   - Schedule kickoff meeting with customer stakeholders and engineering points of contact.
   - Review scope, milestones, success criteria, and SLAs.
   - Deliverables: Project plan, contact list, access matrix.
2) Setup & network (1–4 weeks):
   - Validate VPC peering, firewall rules, and egress requirements for Private deployments.
   - Provision Dedicated capacity or verify hosted API keys and quotas.
   - Deliverables: Connectivity test report, provisioned capacity confirmation.
3) Integration & validation (2–6 weeks):
   - Implement API calls, authentication (API key/OIDC), and telemetry hooks.
   - Run integration test plan (sample prompts, rate tests, per-route SLO checks).
   - Deliverables: Integration test results, sandbox evaluation report.
4) Performance tuning & cost optimization (2–4 weeks):
   - Run workload profiling to recommend batching, KV cache settings, quantization profile, and routing rules.
   - Deliverables: Optimize runbook and expected token-cost delta.
5) Launch & Handoff (1 week):
   - Finalize roll-out plan, enable production keys, and execute cutover checklist.
   - Handoff to support and account team with runbooks and playbooks.

Integration checklist (must pass before production cutover):
- Authentication validated: API keys or OIDC flow tested.
- Rate limiting and quotas applied with test traffic at 1.2x expected burst.
- Observability hooks: request IDs, latency tracking, and error tracing enabled.
- Logging & audit: customer logs integrated into their SIEM where required.
- Telemetry: token-level cost reporting enabled for first 30 days.
- Security: KMS integration (if required) and key rotation policy documented.
- Routing: fallback model and routing policy configured (hosted <-> dedicated).
- Rollback plan documented with safe time window and contact list.

Sample integration test commands and snippets:
- Curl sample generation call:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model": "redwood-mini-1", "input": "Hello world"}'

- Load test guidance:
  - Start at 25% expected RPS for 15 minutes, validate latency p50/p95/p99 and error rate < 1%.
  - Ramp to 100% in 20 minutes, validate autoscaling and quota behaviour.

Escalation playbook (for critical customer-impact incidents):
- Priorities and definitions:
  - P0 (Service down / data loss): immediate exec notification, 24/7 response.
  - P1 (Major feature broken / severe degradation): response goal 1 hour business hours, 2 hours off-hours.
  - P2 (Partial degradation / repeatable error): response goal 4 business hours.
  - P3 (Minor / request for information): next-business-day response.

- Escalation steps (ordered):
  1. Triage at first contact (Tier 1): collect request-id, customer region, model & version, sequence length, and sample payload.
  2. Reproduce in staging or instrumented sandbox with identical parameters (SE/Support).
  3. If P0/P1: page on-call SRE and runtime engineering immediately using the on-call matrix.
  4. Open an internal incident in Incident Manager with summary, timeline, and affected customers.
  5. Assign action owners and timelines; update customer every 30 minutes for P0 and hourly for P1.
  6. Post-incident: run a triage and RCA within 72 hours; create follow-up tasks and track in JIRA.

Escalation contact matrix (short):
- Tier 1 Support: support@redwood.ai / Slack #support (Mon–Fri 9–6 PT)
- SD/SE on-call: paged via PagerDuty (owner: eng-platform)
- Serving runtime on-call (P0): on-call SRE (owner: eng-sre)
- Executive escalation: CSM + Head of Customer Success (owner: customer-success leadership)

SLOs and monitoring expectations (recommended defaults to include in onboarding):
- Availability SLO: 99.9% monthly for hosted endpoints; Dedicated contracts to set SLA in contract.
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 150ms, p95 < 350ms for conversational models under expected load (subject to model/seq length).
- Error rate target: <1% 4xx/5xx aggregated.
- Alert thresholds: p95 latency > 2x baseline for 5m, or error rate > 3% for 5m.

Known issues and workarounds (selected, with detection and mitigation):
- Issue: KV cache invalidation after model rollback causing increased latency.
  Workaround: Clear per-customer cache in the dashboard and temporarily route to fallback model until cache repopulates.
- Issue: High memory OOM on large-sequence jobs with older kernels.
  Workaround: Pin to newer kernel build (v2.4+) or reduce max_sequence by 25% and enable streaming.
- Issue: Intermittent 429s during global bursts when routing policy is misconfigured.
  Workaround: Update routing policy to allow short-term burst capacity and enable client retries with exponential backoff (max 3 attempts).
- Issue: Token-cost spikes after switching quantization profile.
  Workaround: Re-run workload profiler against production traffic in a sandbox, revert profile if cost delta > 15% without quality improvement.

Customer-facing runbooks and handoff artifacts (deliver at launch):
- Customer runbook: incident steps, contact list, and cutover checklist (PDF).
- Integration summary: API endpoints, example calls, quotas, and whitelisted IPs.
- Optimize recommendations: batching/cache/quantization guidance and expected cost savings.
- SLA and escalation flow: clear steps and communication cadence for P0/P1 incidents.

QBR & health-check template (30/60/90+ cadence):
- Executive summary: adoption metrics, major wins, and risks.
- Usage & cost: tokens consumed by route, cost per 1k tokens, anomalies.
- Performance: latency p50/p95/p99, error rates, incidents since last QBR.
- Quality & accuracy: regression tests on canonical prompt sets, recent model changes and eval results.
- Roadmap & requests: upcoming Redwood features that affect the customer, ask backlog items.
- Action items & owners: list of next steps with owners and target dates.

Template: For each customer QBR include the following one-page summary section as the first slide:
- Customer Health (Green/Yellow/Red) with one-line rationale
- Top 3 metrics (Usage, Cost per 1k tokens, p95 latency)
- Current open escalations and status
- Top 3 recommendations and estimated impact

Reporting and audit retention guidance:
- Keep detailed incident timelines and postmortems for 12 months (owner: eng-sre + customer-success).
- Usage and billing logs retained for 24 months (owner: Finance & Billing).
- Security evidence (KMS rotations, access logs) retained per customer-specific contract.

Operational handoffs and ownership matrix (brief):
- Provisioning and network validation: Solutions Engineering (owner: eng-private-deployments)
- Runtime performance tuning: Applied ML & Runtime teams (owner: eng-serving-runtime)
- Incident response and on-call: SRE and eng-platform (owner: eng-sre)
- Billing and quotas: Finance & Billing (owner: finance-and-legal)
- Customer success and QBRs: Customer Success (owner: customer-success)

Appendix A — Example cutover checklist (production launch):
- Confirm access on production API keys and rotate staging keys.
- Run smoke tests at 10 RPS for 5 minutes; validate 200 responses and p95 within SLO.
- Validate logging & request ID propagation in customer dashboards.
- Confirm billing and quota settings for production tiers.
- Communicate change window and rollback window.

Appendix B — Postmortem & RCA requirements:
- For P0 incidents produce a formal postmortem in Confluence within 72 hours including timeline, impact, root cause, corrective actions, and preventive measures.
- Assign owners and link follow-up JIRA tickets.

Notes and references:
- See related architecture and network requirements in /confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides.
- For model rollout policies and canary guidance see /confluence/eng-platform/rollouts.

If significant changes are required to this playbook (new escalation steps, SLA changes, or new integration requirements), update this page and notify reviewers.
